state.scope:
Parent: #1022. Baseline observation: CORE-01 (P1). Depends on delivered #1028/#1029.

Observable gap: fourteen aggregate guards serialize statically typed DomainEvent as `{}`. Several other nominal payload budgets exceed the pinned Fitz operation limit. FitzEventStore serializes after opening an append session and can begin a batch before finding an oversized later event. KV writes need real route/key/value overhead.

Allowed scope: shared concrete generated event sizing; corrections to audited event guards/budgets; shared whole-attributed-batch event-store preflight and notifier forwarding; KV write framing guard; transport-independent validation mapping; application composition; focused regressions and serializer/SDK boundary proof; remediation ledger updates. No aggregate boundary split, business-policy change, new lifetime cap, unrelated identity contract, deployment or environment reset.

Acceptance:
- Focused RED before implementation, starting with oversized concrete incident event admitted by individually valid fields.
- Preflight all actual serialized envelopes before any append session opens; enforce `envelope bytes + UTF8(route) + 26 <= 65535` and KV `value + route + key + 20 <= 65535`.
- Reject oversized later events before any batch append, including large attribution, Unicode and serializer failures; preserve exact valid-boundary batches, read paths, cancellation and event notifications.
- Oversize rejection maps to ordinary nontransient request validation for result/no-result dispatch without bypassing authorization.
- Replace the fourteen base-event calls; correct additional nominal budgets; use concrete generated metadata with coverage of affected event types.
- Focused/full backend units, format, Release build, bounded Jev design and immutable-head preflight, adversarial review, final-head CI, squash merge and readback.

Stopping point: CORE-01 persistence safety delivered and source-backed coverage recorded; the structural content splits remain in their owning later families.

streamAppend.operationPayloadFormula: 8 sessionId +8 expectedOffset +4 bodyLength +E serializedEventEnvelope +1 metadataFlag +4 metadataLength +R UTF8(streamRoute) +1 discriminatorFlag = E+R+26
streamAppend.eventEnvelopeIncludes: Portia discriminator name/version, serialized DomainEventMetadata and concrete event payload; a domain-payload-only gate does not measure full envelope.

kvWrite.operationPayloadFormula: 8 transactionId +4 routeLength +R routeUTF8 +4 keyLength +K keyBytes +4 valueLength +V valueBytes =V+R+K+20
kvWrite.note: KvPut104 has one-byte opcode; correlated transport adds14 bytes. Generic MaxFrameSize65551 is not a value limit.

evidence.claim: EncodeCorrelated applies same65535 operation payload ceiling.
Append operation constructs sessionId+offset+body length/body+metadata flag/length+metadata+discriminator flag.
Whole operation payload goes to StreamAppend.
Request bytes pass through FrameCodec.Encode or EncodeCorrelated.
Actual durable event serializes runtime payload plus discriminator/version and metadata envelope.
Portia includes stream route metadata on each append and passes full serialized event body.
KV writes encode txId,route,key length/key,value length/value before codec.

pinnedConstraints.budgetConsequence: 64KiB=65536 already exceeds65535 operation bytes before ANY Portia envelope/append metadata.128/256/384/512KiB thresholds are incompatible with one Fitz record even after fixing base type erasure.48KiB and32KiB concrete payload budgets leave margin but are not exact envelope/frame proof.

state.observed: 14 factories return DomainEvent or Fits receives DomainEvent; default generic JSON yields {}. Other guards have 64-512KiB budgets. AggregateRepository stamps attribution before IEventStore.AppendAsync. FitzEventStore opens a session before serializing each event. Core generated JSON context already lists audited concrete event contracts.
state.candidateA: Use runtime event type with Core generated JsonTypeInfo for the existing aggregate guards; 48KiB payload budget as an early storage margin. Wrap IEventStore to serialize and size the entire attributed batch before delegating, forwarding reads and IDomainEventNotifier. Wrap IKvClient transactions to validate Insert/Put using actual route and key bytes; map stream oversize exceptions through a shared IRequestBus wrapper after normal authorization. Preserve original service lifetimes with keyed registrations.
state.candidateB: Only change generic serialization in aggregates; use 65536 as payload ceiling; rely on Fitz codec errors after session opens.
state.candidateC: Change every factory and call site to generic Emit<TEvent> with JsonTypeInfo and still add exact attributed-batch storage guard.
state.accepted: Do not alter aggregate business boundaries or approval policies in this slice. No new lifetime caps or broad compatibility paths. Serializer failures must fail before any append; unknown internal serializer errors are not client validation.

design.instructions: Which candidate most directly provides full pinned-transport safety in this bounded slice with least unnecessary call-site churn?

criteria.A: Runtime generated event metadata at aggregate guards, whole attributed batch preflight, exact KV overhead and consistent result mapping.
criteria.B: Only aggregate generic JSON replacement and a 65536-byte payload cap.
criteria.C: Generic factory conversion of every call site plus whole-batch guard.
criteria.needs_refinement: No candidate meets accepted scope/safety because of a concrete missing contract.

validationBoundary.instructions: Which exceptions should the shared request result bridge classify as client validation?

criteria.known_stream_limit: Only a known preflight stream-frame oversize rejection before any append in that batch; preserve authorization, cancellation, concurrency and serializer failures.
criteria.all_persistence_errors: Every event-store/KV/serialization exception, including projector failures and unknown outcomes.
criteria.none: Never return validation for an oversize authored event; propagate every size rejection as an unhandled exception.
